chapters.title: Chapter 4721: Depth! V
paragraphs: The action was a glorious and heavy one!

Noah had come here prepared for battle. He had expected to test his Thesis against Fundamental Depth resistance, to see how his Archai performed under pressure, to learn the limits of his Formless Depth through conflict! Instead, his enemy had simply... surrendered.
It felt anticlimactic.
It felt-
WUU!
At such a pivotal moment, a terrifying aura bloomed.
Noah’s eyes flashed coldly as even though he moved, it was still too fast.
It was Half-Step Absolute Depth making a move, and it was undeniable.
BOOM!
Before anything could even be perceived or seen, an immense pressure smacked Noah from the skies and forcefully pushed him down. The weight was beyond anything Gal’Thûrak had produced!
It was gravity multiplied by authority multiplied by the sheer immensity of a being that stood half a step from the absolute peak of existence.
A Declaration bloomed in the skies above, words of power that rewrote local reality with the casual ease of breathing.
"Only those with my permission can remain floating."
BOOM!
It was a heavy and profound Declaration!
Noah’s body plummeted.

The Arche of Perpetual Harvest worked frantically to convert the incoming force, but even at any percentage conversion, the remaining percentage was staggering. His Formless Depth screamed that he should be able to resist this, that normal rules didn’t apply to him, but the gap between Intermediate and Half-Step Absolute was not a gap that could be bridged through quality alone.
Not yet.

His feet hit the obsidian flaming earth of Muspelheim with force that sent shockwaves rippling outward. A crater formed beneath him, spreading cracks through the primordial stone that had existed since before differentiation. Flames erupted around him, responding to the violence of his landing with sympathetic fury.
And there he stood.

His figure shone with defiance in the heart of that crater. Blue-gold light crackled across his body, his Mana responding to the assault with instinctive resistance. His robes of crystallized starlight had torn in places, revealing skin that gleamed with the same azure-golden luminescence. His hair whipped around his face from residual force, and his eyes blazed with light that refused to dim.
He did not stumble.
He did not fall.

He stood in that crater as if he had chosen to be there, as if the earth of Muspelheim should be honored to support his weight, as if being forced from the sky was merely an inconvenience rather than a humiliation!
And he calmly raised his head to look above.
THE Living Spirit had appeared near Gal’Thûrak.

The entity was massive in a way that transcended physical dimension. Its form was composed of countless spirits compressed into a singular presence, faces and limbs and eyes all merged into something that was both one and many simultaneously. It burned with power that made the eternal flames of Muspelheim seem like candles, and its attention pressed down upon reality with weight that warped space itself.
This was Half-Step Absolute Depth.
This was what stood between the Fundamental and the true peak.
This was his true enemy.
|Declaration Impact Analysis|
|Declaration: "Only those with my permission can remain floating."|
|Source: THE Living Spirit (Half-Step Absolute Depth)|
|Effect: Forced grounding of all entities within Declaration radius who lack explicit permission.|
|Your Status: Grounded. The Declaration overrode your spatial positioning through raw authority differential.|
|Damage Assessment: Against anything with a glimmer of Absolute Depth, you still require unique means to stand against them. The immensity of their Depths is incalculable by normal standards.|
|Even with your Thesis in place, even with your Formless Depth and glorious Foundation, 40% of your existence’s integrity was affected and destabilized by the power of THE Living Spirit.|

|Current Recovery: Existence stabilizing. Damage converting to experience. The Arche of Perpetual Harvest is doing its best, but there’s only so much it can harvest from being slapped out of the sky like a particularly ambitious insect.|
| THE Living Spirit is testing you. He wanted to see how you’d respond to overwhelming force after his subordinate’s submission denied him information. You are currently providing that information.|
As THE Living Spirit stared down at Noah from above, he reached out with one of his countless limbs and smacked his kneeling follower with casual contempt.
The blow sent Gal’Thûrak sliding across the burning sky, his chains rattling as he absorbed the impact.
"Grow a spine,"THE Living Spirit said, his voice emerging from a thousand mouths simultaneously, "and never kneel again. The enemy is merely at Fundamental Depth."
BOOM!

Gal’Thûrak rose from where he had been struck, his seven eyes opening one by one as he straightened his massive form. The chains around him began to rattle once more, though with noticeably less enthusiasm than before.

"Sir didn’t answer when I called out before,"Gal’Thûrak said, his voice calm despite the blow he had just received. "It almost seemed like you wanted me to sacrifice my Way to gather information about this enemy."
THE Living Spirit glared at Gal’Thûrak with cold fury.

The accusation hung in the air between them, unspoken but understood. Yes, that was exactly what THE Living Spirit had wanted. Yes, he had been willing to let his subordinate be destroyed if it meant learning the enemy’s capabilities. And yes, Gal’Thûrak had seen through the strategy and chosen self-preservation over loyal sacrifice.
Neither of them acknowledged it directly.
Neither of them needed to.
Their gazes turned toward Noah.
And Noah stared back at them.

The region around him vibrated and trembled as his existence worked to repair itself. He could feel the damage the Declaration had caused, the destabilization that rippled through his foundation like cracks in glass. It wasn’t critical. It wasn’t permanent. But it was a reminder that Half-Step Absolute Depth was not something he could face casually.
Not with his current immensity.
Not with his current weight.

He stretched, rolling his shoulders as blue-gold light flickered across his form. The cracks in his existence sealed themselves, his Formless Depth refusing to accept the damage as anything more than temporary inconvenience. His Arche of Perpetual Harvest worked continuously, converting the ambient power of Muspelheim into resources that fueled his recovery.
And then he waved his hand.
From his body, from the deepest reserves where he kept his most precious assets, he pulled out a radiant marble.
BOOM!
The momentThe Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhememerged into open air, a shuddering aura erupted outward.

Reality itself seemed to recoil from the object. The flames of Muspelheim flickered in confusion, unsure whether they should burn brighter or extinguish entirely. The obsidian earth beneath Noah’s feet cracked further, not from force but from fundamental instability. Even the weight of THE Living Spirit’s Declaration seemed to waver, as if the local laws of reality were suddenly negotiable.
THE Living Spirit’s gaze changed.
The countless eyes that composed his form all focused on that marble with intensity that hadn’t been present before. He recognized what Noah held!
But Noah remained gloriously calm and defiant in the face of this terrifyingly powerful enemy.

He held The Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem loosely, almost carelessly, as if it were a toy rather than a piece of one of the fundamental truths that governed existence. His eyes met THE Living Spirit’s countless gazes without flinching.
And he smiled.
"Let’s have a bit of Mayhem, shall we?"
BOOM!
|Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem - Activation Sequence|
|An unfathomable weight of your Way is being committed to activate the Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem.|
|This is not a small expenditure.|
|Activation Status: Initiating.|

|Effect Upon Full Activation: Targetted entities within range will experience temporary Depth reduction. THE Living Spirit’s Half-Step Absolute Depth will be pulled down. Gal’Thûrak’s already diminished capability will crater further. The playing field will be forcibly leveled through the introduction of fundamental chaos into the local hierarchy of power.|
|Mayhem is easy to start. It’s considerably harder to survive.|
WAA!

chapters.title: Chapter 4722: It Is Not Enough I
paragraphs: Capítulo 4722: It Is Not Enough I
Mayhem.

It was a word that held weight far beyond its simple syllables. It stood for disorder and destruction, of systems breaking down and certainties crumbling into dust. It was the promise that nothing built could last forever, that every structure would eventually fall, that every order would eventually dissolve into the formless chaos from which it emerged.
Many entities feared mayhem.

They built walls against it. They constructed hierarchies and laws and Principles designed to hold it at bay. They convinced themselves that through sufficient power, sufficient order, sufficient control, they could keep the chaos outside their domains forever.
They were wrong.
In the end, everything flowed toward chaos and entropy.

This was not nihilism. This was simply the fundamental truth of existence itself. Order required energy to maintain. Structure demanded constant effort to preserve. But chaos? Chaos was the default state. Chaos was what remained when effort ceased. Chaos was patient in a way that order could never be, because chaos did not need to do anything except wait.
And chaos always won eventually.

THE Creature represented existence itself, the foundational truth that things were.
THE Living Paradox represented contradiction, the impossible truth that things could be and not be simultaneously.
But THE Primordial Chaos represented the end state of all things. The destination toward which every river of existence inevitably flowed. The final answer to every question ever asked.
Entropy.
Dissolution.
The return to...formlessness.

His power did not need to be flashy. It did not need to be dramatic. It simply needed to be patient, because time itself was his ally. Every moment that passed brought all of existence one increment closer to the chaos he embodied. Every structure that formed was already in the process of falling apart. Every order that arose was already beginning to decay.
THE Primordial Chaos did not need to win battles.
He simply needed to wait for everyone else to lose.
At this time, the clearest depiction of mayhem and what chaos could do could be seen in the Wastes of THE Fallout.
Away from the heavy conflict in Muspelheim.
Away from the unmentioned and unknown and ongoing battles between THE Creature and THE Living Paradox.
In the Wastes of THE Fallout, multiple Declarations of THE Fundamental Depth entities permeated as the battle between THE First Leader, Gilgamesh, and Lumivara unfolded.
The landscape itself had been torn apart by the conflict!

What had once been regions of ash and volcanic flame now bore the scars of conceptual warfare. Craters the size of small realms marked where Declarations had clashed against Declarations. Rifts in space itself showed where the weight of Fundamental Depth had proven too heavy for reality to bear. The air shimmered with residual authority, fragments of power that had nowhere to go now that the Declarations that spawned them had been shattered.
Lumivara stood at the center of a devastated plain, her nine tails spread behind her like broken banners of war.
No.
Not nine tails.
Seven.

Two had been severed earlier in the battle, their stumps still leaking crimson gold blood that hissed where it touched the corrupted ground. Her radiant humanoid form, which had always blazed with the brilliance of captured starlight, now flickered with the uncertainty of a flame. Her fox-like features, usually so sharp and beautiful, were twisted with pain and defiance.
And across her chest, a huge gash wept crimson gold blood in steady rivers.

The Way of Unity had been carved into her flesh alongside the physical damage, and that conceptual wound rejected the union of her very cells. Her body wanted to heal. Her Principles demanded regeneration. But the Declaration that had inflicted the injury insisted that what had been separated could not be rejoined.
Around her, Declarations of her own blazed in defensive formation.
“My Light shall blind all who seek to harm me.”
“My radiance burns with the fury of Mana.”
“Within my presence, darkness cannot approach.”

Each Declaration was a masterwork of Fundamental Depth authority. Each one would have been enough to annihilate armies of lesser entities. Each one represented the culmination of eons of cultivation, of refinement, of pushing the Way of Light to heights that few had ever achieved.
Her power should have been more than enough to wipe the floor with any common THE Fundamental Depth entity.
But she did not face a common one now!
She faced Gilgamesh!

THE First Leader stood forty meters away, his form radiating authority that predated civilizations. Golden hair shone upon a face that had worn crowns when crowns still meant something. His armor of paradoxical gold and obsidian shifted between states of being, solid and ethereal simultaneously, as if unable to decide what it truly was.
Around him, crimson gold weapons floated in perfect formation.

Swords and spears and axes and halberds, each one carrying heavy and immense Declarations of its own. They orbited his form like planets around a sun, waiting to be called upon, eager to taste blood once more.
One spear in particular leaked crimson gold luminescence.
Lumivara’s blood.
The blood from the wound across her chest.
And the Declarations that surrounded Gilgamesh made her own seem like children’s prayers by comparison.
“All treasures belong to the King.”
“That which is divided shall be unified under my authority.”
“Paradox bends to my will, for I am THE First Leader.”
“Unity is inevitable within my presence.”

The Way of Unity, backed by Paradox itself, pressed against Lumivara’s defenses with weight that made the air itself groan. Where her Light pushed outward in radiant defiance, his Unity pulled inward with gravitational certainty. Where her Declarations insisted on separation and independence, his Declarations demanded convergence and submission.
His forces stood at a distance, eighteen Early Creatures with their obsidian spears and paradoxical armor.
They did not make a move.
They did not need to!
Their Leader faced Lumivara himself, and that was more than sufficient.

Gilgamesh looked at the wounded fox with eyes that held something almost like respect. Almost like pity. His expression was calm, measured, the face of a king who had seen countless enemies fall before him and would see countless more.
“It seems you are much more familiar with Mana than the others were.”
His voice carried across the devastated plain, each word weighted with ancient authority.

“The ones we captured, the ones whose heads now adorn my subordinates’ spears, they had only the faintest glimmers of that blue-gold thread. But you...” He tilted his head, studying her. “You are saturated with it. It flows through your Way like blood through veins.”
He stepped forward, and the weapons around him shifted in response.
“Are you close with Osmont? Do you remember him fondly?”
The questions were casual, conversational, as if they were not standing in the aftermath of a battle that had reshaped the landscape.
“How would he react should you perish here? Should you be collapsed entirely, your Way scattered across the Wastes like ash in the wind?”
He paused, and something that might have been genuine consideration crossed his features.
“It would be a shame to collapse you. Let us not do that. I have no issue with you personally, little fox. You are merely a means to an end.”
His hand reached out, and the blood-stained spear floated to his grasp.
“So just... call upon Osmont. Tell him you need him to come save you. As a Leader, he will come.”
His eyes met hers, and for a moment, something ancient and heavy passed between them.

“All of us Leaders... we bear this heaviness and weight. We cannot abandon those who follow us, even when wisdom demands we stay away. It is our blessing and our curse. Call him, and this can end without your collapse.”
Lumivara looked at this ancient king, this being of incomprehensible power who had cornered her so thoroughly.
She looked at the blood leaking from her chest, at the stumps where two of her tails had been, at the devastation that surrounded them both.
She patted her chest.

The movement sent fresh waves of agony through her existence, but she did it anyway. Her hand came away coated in crimson gold blood, thick and luminescent and carrying the essence of her Way within it.
And she wiped that blood across her face.
Like war paint!
Like a declaration of her own!
Her eyes met Gilgamesh’s, and despite the pain, despite the exhaustion, despite the overwhelming certainty of her defeat, they blazed with defiance that refused to dim.
“Just fight, you motherfucker.”

chapters.title: Chapter 4723: It Is Not Enough II
paragraphs: For a long moment, Gilgamesh simply stared at her.
Then he sighed.
It was a heavy sound, filled with something that might have been disappointment or might have been respect or might have been both intertwined so thoroughly that even he couldn’t separate them.
"Very well."
He raised his hand, and the weapons around him began to spin faster.
Lumivara responded with everything she had left.
"MY TAILS ARE THE SHARPEST IN EXISTENCE, AND THEY SHALL PIERCE EVERYTHING BEFORE ME!"
BOOM!

The Declaration erupted from her with force that cracked the ground beneath her feet. Her seven remaining tails blazed with light so intense that the Wastes themselves recoiled, and then they transformed. No longer flowing extensions of her form, they became blades of concentrated radiance, each one carrying the full weight of her Way behind it.
They surged toward Gilgamesh like the wrath of dying Folds.

The very Wastes were torn by their passage. Space itself split where they traveled, unable to contain the sharpness she had declared into existence. Ash and flame and corrupted matter all fell away before her assault, annihilated by light that refused to acknowledge any obstacle.
Gilgamesh watched them come.
His eyes shone with immensity, with the weight of eons, with the accumulated authority of a being who had stood at the pinnacle of existence since before most entities learned to crawl.
And with pity.
"ALL THAT IS DIVIDED SHALL BE UNIFIED. ALL THAT IS MANY SHALL BECOME ONE. ALL THAT OPPOSES ME SHALL JOIN ME OR CEASE."
BOOM!
His Declaration unfolded with force that made Lumivara’s seem like a whisper against a hurricane.
The Way of Unity, backed by the full weight of THE First Leader’s existence, crashed against her bladed tails with absolute authority. It did not deflect them. It did not block them. It unified them!
What had been seven became one.
What had been sharp became dull.
What had been an attack became... nothing.
SNAP!

Her tails, all seven of them, were bisected simultaneously as Gilgamesh’s Declaration cut through her own like a blade through silk. The sharpness she had declared was unified into a single point that collapsed under its own conceptual weight. The light she had summoned was unified into a darkness that could not illuminate anything.
And Gilgamesh himself moved forward.
His hand grasped the blood-stained spear with casual ease, and he crossed the distance between them in a single step that seemed to last forever.
The spear thrust toward Lumivara’s heart- towards her Heart of Light.

She roared with defiance even as the blood from her bisected tails ran down her form in crimson gold rivers. Even as her remaining tails, now stumps that wept luminescence, thrashed uselessly behind her. Even as every part of her existence screamed that this was the end!
Crimson gold tears leaked from her eyes, mixing with the blood she had painted across her face.
And in that moment, she did not think of escape. She did not think of survival. She did not think of the battle or the enemy or the pain that consumed her existence.
She thought of her master.

Of the entity who had given her Mana when she had only Light. Who had elevated her from a minor thing in The Infinite Unfurling to someone who could eventually stand against Fundamental Depth entities. Who had held her like the little fox she had been, stroking her fur.
She just wanted to see him again.
To be held by him one more time.
To hear his voice telling her that she had done well.
The spear came closer, its point gleaming with inevitability.
And Gilgamesh’s voice rang out from all around, heavy with the weight of a king who had witnessed too many endings.
"Sometimes... we try and try our best. And sometimes, it is not enough."
His words carried no mockery or satisfaction. Only ancient understanding.
"It is not to say you were lacking. Your Way is brilliant. Your determination is admirable. Your loyalty to your master is something I can respect."
The spear reached within inches of her chest.
"Sometimes, Existence is just really unfair."
His eyes met hers one final time.
"Rest, little fox. I will find your master another way."
At such a time!
At such a pivotal moment where it looked like Lumivara’s fate was sealed!
A voice boomed across the Wastes of THE Fallout.
"Yes, sometimes, Existence is unfair..."
Gilgamesh’s eyes widened.
His spear, inches from Lumivara’s heart, stopped.
And it was not because he chose to stop it, but because something stopped it for him!
BOOM!

Boundless waves of obsidian goldhairdescended from above like a curtain of judgment. Each strand carried weight that made Gilgamesh’s weapons tremble. Each fiber blazed with Mana so dense and pure that the corrupted Wastes themselves seemed to recoil from its presence.
The hair crashed against Gilgamesh’s crimson gold weapons, and those treasures that had conquered civilizations shattered like glass against stone!
An impenetrable wall formed between Gilgamesh and his prey.
Hair woven so densely that light itself could not pass through. Hair that thrummed with Declarations of its own, Declarations that made both Lumivara’s and Gilgamesh’s seem modest by comparison.
And beside that vibrant obsidian gold wall, a figure appeared next to Lumivara.
He was covered entirely in hair.

Obsidian gold strands flowed from every inch of his form, cascading around him like a living cloak that responded to his will. The hair moved with purpose, with intention, with the casual authority of someone who had long since stopped needing to prove anything to anyone. Where it touched the corrupted ground of the Wastes, the corruption fled.

Waves of obsidian Undifferentiated Mana surrounded him like an endless sea, so dense and pure that it seemed less like energy and more like liquid existence given form. The air itself bent around his presence, not in fear but in acknowledgment. Reality recognized this being and treated him with the deference reserved for those who had transcended normal hierarchies.
His face could not be seen beneath the curtain of hair.
But somehow, somehow, one could almost envision him smiling at this moment.
Lumivara looked toward this hairy figure with a tear-stricken face.
Shock and then recognition bloomed in her eyes. Disbelief. Hope. And then something that might have been called joy if joy could be mixed with relief so profound that it bordered on collapse!
She lunged toward him.

Her wounded form, bleeding from a dozen injuries, missing two tails entirely, carved with the Way of Unity that rejected her healing, threw itself at this figure with abandon that spoke of absolute trust.
She embraced him!
Her arms wrapped around his hairy form, and her face pressed against his chest as sobs wracked her body!
The hairy entity stood there for a moment, accepting her embrace as he sighed!
After all, the two of them had been in THE Belly of Existence for a long, long time.
His hairy hand rose and stroked the head of the little fox with gentleness that seemed impossible for someone radiating such immense power.
"There, there."
His voice was warm and comforting, holding the weight of someone who had arrived exactly when he was needed and knew it.
"It’s okay."
He continued to stroke her hair as she cried against him, her tears mixing with the blood that covered her form as he let her have this moment.
Then he turned toward Gilgamesh.

The hairy figure regarded THE First Leader with what might have been curiosity or might have been contempt or might have been simple assessment, his face remaining hidden beneath that curtain of obsidian gold while the weight of his attention pressed down upon the ancient king with unmistakable authority.
"Why would a Leader be bullying a child?"
The words carried across the devastated plain with casual authority that made the air itself tremble.
And then...
BOOM!
An unbelievably immense force shining obsidian gold smashed into Gilgamesh with violence that defied comprehension!
It was not an attack in any conventional sense but simply pressure, the weight of existence itself deciding that Gilgamesh should not be standing where he was standing.
Gilgamesh’s massive and unbeatable figure was flung backward like a leaf caught in a hurricane!

He who had conquered civilizations, he who had stood against armies, he who had made Lumivara seem like a child before his authority despite her being a Fundamental Depth entity saturated with Mana, was sent careening through the corrupted air of the Wastes with no ability to resist or slow his trajectory!
When he finally stopped, cratering into the corrupted Wastes with force that sent shockwaves rippling outward for miles, one could see his forehead.
It was cracked.

A single fissure ran from his hairline to his brow, splitting the perfect features that had worn crowns as crimson gold Unity flowed from the wound like blood from a mortal injury, the essence of his Way leaking from him in steady streams that spoke of damage far deeper than the physical.
And it did not heal.
The crack remained stubborn and impossible, refusing to close despite the immense regenerative capabilities that someone of his Depth should possess, a testament to the power that had inflicted it!
His gaze turned heavy and somber as he rose from the crater of Wastes, his ancient eyes focusing on the hairy figure standing beside Lumivara with an intensity of reassessment and recalculation.
He looked at that impossible entity, and understanding dawned in his ancient eyes.
From the light that had smashed into him, from the pressure that had flung him backward, from the wound that refused to close despite everything his Way of Unity demanded...
He could sense a glimmer of Absolute.

It was not fully Absolute, not the complete and total authority of someone who had reached the true peak of existence, but it was a glimmer, a taste, a promise of what lay within that hairy form that could not be ignored or dismissed!
And this...
This was heavy.
Truly, truly heavy!

For the first time since the battle began, for the first time since he had cornered Lumivara and demanded she call upon her master, for the first time since he had declared his intention to find Noah Osmont through any means necessary...
Gilgamesh looked upon an enemy and felt uncertainty.
At this moment, Ul’moreth, THE Primeval Titan, had arrived.

After all, the two of them had been in THE Belly of Existence for a long, long time.
His hairy hand rose and stroked the head of the little fox with gentleness that seemed impossible for someone radiating such immense power.
"There, there."
His voice was warm and comforting, holding the weight of someone who had arrived exactly when he was needed and knew it.
"It’s okay."
He continued to stroke her hair as she cried against him, her tears mixing with the blood that covered her form as he let her have this moment.
Then he turned toward Gilgamesh.

The hairy figure regarded THE First Leader with what might have been curiosity or might have been contempt or might have been simple assessment, his face remaining hidden beneath that curtain of obsidian gold while the weight of his attention pressed down upon the ancient king with unmistakable authority.
"Why would a Leader be bullying a child?"
The words carried across the devastated plain with casual authority that made the air itself tremble.
And then...
BOOM!
An unbelievably immense force shining obsidian gold smashed into Gilgamesh with violence that defied comprehension!
It was not an attack in any conventional sense but simply pressure, the weight of existence itself deciding that Gilgamesh should not be standing where he was standing.
Gilgamesh’s massive and unbeatable figure was flung backward like a leaf caught in a hurricane!

He who had conquered civilizations, he who had stood against armies, he who had made Lumivara seem like a child before his authority despite her being a Fundamental Depth entity saturated with Mana, was sent careening through the corrupted air of the Wastes with no ability to resist or slow his trajectory!
When he finally stopped, cratering into the corrupted Wastes with force that sent shockwaves rippling outward for miles, one could see his forehead.
It was cracked.

A single fissure ran from his hairline to his brow, splitting the perfect features that had worn crowns as crimson gold Unity flowed from the wound like blood from a mortal injury, the essence of his Way leaking from him in steady streams that spoke of damage far deeper than the physical.
And it did not heal.
The crack remained stubborn and impossible, refusing to close despite the immense regenerative capabilities that someone of his Depth should possess, a testament to the power that had inflicted it!
His gaze turned heavy and somber as he rose from the crater of Wastes, his ancient eyes focusing on the hairy figure standing beside Lumivara with an intensity of reassessment and recalculation.
He looked at that impossible entity, and understanding dawned in his ancient eyes.
From the light that had smashed into him, from the pressure that had flung him backward, from the wound that refused to close despite everything his Way of Unity demanded...
He could sense a glimmer of Absolute.

It was not fully Absolute, not the complete and total authority of someone who had reached the true peak of existence, but it was a glimmer, a taste, a promise of what lay within that hairy form that could not be ignored or dismissed!
And this...
This was heavy.
Truly, truly heavy!

For the first time since the battle began, for the first time since he had cornered Lumivara and demanded she call upon her master, for the first time since he had declared his intention to find Noah Osmont through any means necessary...
Gilgamesh looked upon an enemy and felt uncertainty.
At this moment, Ul’moreth, THE Primeval Titan, had arrived.

chapters.title: Chapter 4724: Against A Legend! I
paragraphs: Axioms had to be truly terrifying things.

Just a Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem allowed for one to lower the Depth of another, and this alone was a capability that could reshape the outcome of any battle, but what did the other Fragments that completed the entire Axiom do? What capabilities lay dormant in the pieces he had not yet obtained? And what could one do with an entire Axiom of Mayhem fully assembled and bent to one’s will?

Noah had such thoughts racing through his mind as he put all his weight on activating a mere Fragment, and even then the process felt impossible, like trying to lift a mountain with hands that were already trembling from exertion.
But something occurred soon after which allowed him to feel a load taken off his shoulders, a weight that had been pressing down upon his reserves suddenly vanishing as if it had never existed.
|Thesis Actualization Complete|
|Your Thesis "Within Muspelheim, only those to whom I grant permission may draw power from The First Tongue" has gone unchallenged.|
|Challenge Window: Expired. No entity attempted dialectic debate against your proposition.|
|Status: Actualized. Your Thesis has solidified into local truth within its coverage area.|
|Previous Maintenance Cost: 67% of available immensity required for active maintenance.|
|Current Maintenance Cost: 0%. The Thesis now maintains itself as an accepted truth of this region.|

|Congratulations, Master. You proposed that you should control who gets to speak reality’s oldest language, and Existence examined your proposition, found no one willing to argue against it, and shrugged in acceptance.|
|Your immensity and weight are now fully available for other applications.|

The moment such a thing occurred, Noah felt his existence pulse with weight and immensity once more as reserves that had been committed to maintaining his Thesis flooded back into his core, filling him with power that had been unavailable just moments before.
He looked at the marble spinning in his grasp, and his eyes shone with blue-gold brilliance as he spoke words that carried the weight of someone who had laid claim to The First Tongue itself.
"The First Tongue commands you, little marble. Don’t believe yourself grander than it."
HUUUUM!

The moment such words boomed out across the burning landscape of Muspelheim, his immensity of THE Formless Depth surged outward and exerted itself onto the Fragment with authority that sought no resistance, and the marble that had been demanding tribute as if it were the superior force began to spin with a crimson obsidian glow that spoke of activation rather than negotiation!
Above, THE Living Spirit looked down with coldness!

And then the light of the Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem flashed out far faster than Planck speed and permeated across this entire region of Muspelheim with inevitability that could not be dodged or blocked or denied!

Noah’s existence began to buzz with sensations that straddled the line between agony and ecstasy, his body trying to lift from the crater he had been thrown into as if gravity itself had decided to reconsider its earlier judgment!
His eyes met THE Living Spirit’s countless gazes, and he smiled with the calm confidence of someone who had always wanted to test himself against such a being and was finally getting his chance.
"I have heard many legends about you. Stories of The Earliest Folds..."
His voice carried across the burning skies, reaching not just THE Living Spirit but his armies and his subordinates and the Muspeli Lifeforms who watched from their positions.

"I always wondered about your fate, and the fate of THE Living Dimensional, THE Living Quantum, THE Living Concept, and even THE Living Temporal." He tilted his head, studying the massive entity before him with genuine curiosity. "Did they stand with THE Creature, or THE Living Paradox? Seeing you moving out here like this all safe and sound... does that mean that you bent the knee to Paradox?"

He broke free from the constraints and floated higher, his robes of crystallized starlight billowing around him as the Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem continued to pulse with crimson obsidian light in his grasp!

"Is the grand Living Spirit moving under his command? Were you told to come here to Muspelheim under the orders of THE Living Paradox? Are there others like you here? Quantum? Concept? That bum fucker Elemental? "
His smile widened, and there was something almost predatory in it now, the expression of someone who had found prey worthy of the hunt.

"You see, I have so many questions, and I don’t think that you are one to give answers freely. So I will take it upon myself today to see if a legend can be cracked, to see if the entities that I used to only hear legends about can be brought low."
He raised his hand, and the Fragment pulsed in response as if eager to demonstrate its capabilities.
"Tell me, O Living Spirit... do you bleed?"

THE Living Spirit looked down at this entity who dared to speak to him in such a manner, this being whose Depth should have made him nothing more than an insect to be crushed, and his countless faces twisted with burning lividity that made the eternal flames of Muspelheim seem cold by comparison.
His form, composed of countless spirits compressed into singular presence, roiled with calm fury that he had not felt in eons!
And yet he could feel it.
The change!
The shift in his existence that the Fragment had wrought.
His weight, his immensity, his Depth that had stood at Half-Step Absolute... something was wrong with it now, something fundamental had been altered by that crimson obsidian light!
At the same time, prompts bloomed before Noah with comprehensive detail.
|Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem - Activation Report|
|An immense concentration of your THE Civilizational Units of Everything has flooded into the Fragment to power its activation on selected targets.|
|THE Organ of Civilization pulses brilliantly as the engine of your Civilization and bears all the cost. Current strain: Significant but sustainable. Your foundation holds firm.|
|Selected Targets and Results:|
|Target 1: THE Living Spirit|
|Original Depth: Half-Step Absolute Depth of Absolute Sovereignty|

|Fragment Effect: Resisted. When two Absolute capabilities meet, complexities bloom. A Fragment of an Axiom is a part of an Absolute, and THE Living Spirit was partly an Absolute himself. The clash of these authorities resulted in partial effect rather than full implementation.|
|Current Depth: Peak of THE Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereignty|

|Assessment: Still terrifyingly powerful, but no longer operating with the weight of someone touching the Absolute. He has been pulled back from the threshold he stood upon. Whether this makes him manageable or merely less impossible remains to be seen.|
|Target 2: Gal’Thûrak THE Subjugator|
|Original Depth: THE Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereignty|
|Fragment Effect: Full implementation. No Absolute qualities to resist.|
|Current Depth: THE Intermediate Depth of Absolute Sovereignty|

|Assessment: That fucker has fallen from Fundamental to Intermediate. Combined with his earlier submission and your Thesis restrictions, he is now operating at a fraction of his former capability.He seems like a good candidate to either kill for multiple Fragments of Moirai Threads or to imprison in THE Infinite Desmoterion.|
|What would having a Fundamental Depth prisoner do for your Way?|
|Additional Targets: The other Fundamental Depth follower of THE Living Spirit surrounding the citadel of flames below has also been affected. They now stand at Intermediate Depth as well.|

|You have just created a target-rich environment of former Fundamental Depth entities who are now within a range you can more feasibly engage. Whether you harvest them for Moirai Threads or collect them for THE Infinite Desmoterion, the options before you are considerably more palatable than they were thirty seconds ago.|

Noah looked at these vibrant prompts and absorbed their implications in an instant, understanding blooming alongside opportunity as he recognized just how dramatically the Fragment had shifted the dynamics of this confrontation.
THE Living Spirit, reduced from Half-Step Absolute to peak Fundamental.
Gal’Thûrak, fallen from Fundamental to Intermediate.
The other Fundamental Depth entities around the citadel, all now standing at Intermediate as well.
An army of legends brought low by a single activation.

He made his move without hesitation, his figure shooting upward with rapidity that left afterimages of blue-gold light trailing behind him as he rocketed toward THE Living Spirit with intent that could not be mistaken for anything other than violence.

He did not underestimate a legend like THE Living Spirit, not even for a moment, because he knew that peak Fundamental Depth was still a height that exceeded his own weight and immensity by significant margins, knew that the countless spirits composing that entity’s form represented eons of accumulated power and knowledge and combat experience.
But at some point, legends fell.
At some point, the stories that had made children tremble and empires kneel became merely that, stories of beings who had once been untouchable but were now bleeding in the dirt like everyone else.
He was more than okay acting as the blade to weed out this legend!

chapters.title: Chapter 4725: Against A Legend! II
paragraphs: A great man once said that those who cling to death, live, and those who cling to life, die.
To live, one had to be ruthless and ready for death at any moment.
To live and thrive in the post-apocalyptic age of THE Fallout, one had to be utterly obscene and prepared for death to come knocking at any time without warning or mercy.

For Noah, it was a simple thing as he was already ruthless and ready for death if it came, had been ready since the first apocalypse came to his tiny blue planet and taught him that existence cared nothing for fairness or justice or the desperate hopes of those who wished to survive!

Every being across existence lived and died, and he had not met any that were impervious to this fact yet, not THE Entities at the highest levels nor the primordial beings that had existed since before differentiation nor even the legends whose names were spoken in whispers across countless realms.
Even THE Primordial Paradox was collapsed, right?!
And THE Living Spirit...
He wanted to see if he could institute this reality for it.

So defiant against the Declaration this being had laid down, defiant against the authority that had smashed him from the skies and forced him into a crater, he rose up against it through sheer will and weight as he breathed out slowly.
Everything slowed down.

When Noah looked up, he saw the cold eyes of THE Living Spirit as the entity gazed down at him with the calm fury of something that had been shown disrespect by a creature it considered beneath notice.

He saw Gal’Thûrak behind and to the side, the demon spirit’s seven eyes wide with an ashen expression as he felt his own Depth diminished, as he recognized what the Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem had done to him, and this being who had called himself THE Terror of Chains actually scrambled backward through the burning air as ifdistancecould save him from what was coming.

Noah saw all of this with clarity that seemed to stretch each moment into eternity, and he raised his left hand with an expression becoming immensely calm, the kind of calm that preceded storms and catastrophes and the ending of things that had seemed eternal.
On his raised hand, a bow began to form.

Blue-gold light crystallized from the ambient Mana of Muspelheim, weaving itself into a weapon that seemed less crafted and more grown, a bow of such elegant lethality! The limbs curved with mathematical perfection, inscribed with Phonemes of The First Tongue that blazed with authority, and the string that connected them thrummed with tension that spoke of violence yearning to be released.

Noah used his right hand to pull on the bow string, his fingers finding their position with the ease of someone who had done this countless times before, and as he drew the string back toward his cheek, a radiant blue-gold arrow began to form between his grip and the bow itself.
The arrow’s edge was sharp beyond sharpness, pointed directly toward THE Living Spirit with intent that could not be mistaken for anything other thanmurder.
How could he be as ruthless as possible here?

The answer was already burning in his mind as he considered his assets, his Thesis that had been actualized, his enemies who could barely access The First Tongue due to that very Thesis, and the opportunity that lay before him like a banquet waiting to be devoured.

His voice echoed out calmly as he declared a new Thesis while tugging at every last drop of immensity he had left within him, building upon the foundation he had already established with brilliance that bordered on cruelty.
"My arrow chains and severs upon all those that can barely access The First Tongue."

His eyes burned with ingenuity as he worked on an already built Thesis to declare such a devastatingly simple proposition, using the restrictions he had already imposed as the framework for something even more horrific!
His enemies could barely access The First Tongue because of his earlier Thesis.
And now his arrow would chain between them, would sever their Ways and their Civilizations with the inevitability of a sentence that had already been written.

His eyes remained locked on THE Living Spirit as he let loose the bow string with a motion that seemed almost gentle, almost casual, as if he were not about to commit an act of mass devastation that would echo across this primordial realm.
And the arrow flew.

Existence distorted around its passage, space itself bending to accommodate something that moved too fast and carried too much weight to be contained by normal physics. A light of established Thesis wrapped around the arrow like a shroud, like a promise, like a death sentence written in blue-gold fire!
Halfway to the cold-faced Living Spirit, the arrow disappeared.
WAP!

This glorious moment stretched in slowed time as Noah and THE Living Spirit continued locked onto each other, their gazes meeting across the burning air of Muspelheim with intensity that made the eternal flames seem cold, the attack Noah had thrown out nowhere to be seen as if it had simply ceased to exist.
And then, horrifically...
OOOOOH!

A furious and horrified roar echoed out from the surroundings of the citadel where the forces of THE Living Spirit had been positioned, a sound of absolute terror from something that had just realized death had arrived without warning or mercy!
Noah’s arrow had not been aimed at THE Living Spirit at all.

It had appeared an inch away from another spirit, one that used to stand at THE Fundamental Depth before The Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem had dragged it down, a monstrous entity whose form resembled a Cetus of ancient legend. Its body was massive and serpentine, scales of gray-white spirit essence covering a form that stretched for miles, with jaws that could have swallowed small realms and eyes that blazed with the fury of oceanic depths that had never known sunlight.

It roared as its Way of Spirit Water tried to make a stand against the arrow that had materialized before its existence, ancient Principles activating in desperate defense as Declarations attempted to form around its body like shields.
But an earlier Thesis had already cut off its access to The First Tongue.
And this arrow carried a Thesis that built upon that previous Thesis while holding a weight no Intermediate Depth entity could truly withstand!

The Cetus had been Fundamental, had stood at heights that would have made it nearly untouchable under normal circumstances, but currently it was dragged down to Intermediate by the Fragment’s power, and what occurred next was just utter devastation of a Way!
It seemed like a long time, but all of this was happening in a fraction of a femtosecond.

The arrow burning with Thesis pierced across the Cetus with the ease of a blade through mist, its blue-gold radiance carving through spirit essence and Way alike as if they were made of paper rather than the accumulated authority of eons. The great serpentine form shuddered once, twice, and then its Way shattered like glass struck by a hammer, fragments of Spirit Water scattering across Muspelheim in a display that would have been beautiful if it were not so terrible.

Its Civilization collapsed in the same instant, the connections it had built over countless years severing all at once as its existence ceased to be anything more than resources waiting to be harvested.
And then the arrow flew ever faster.
It did not stop with a single kill.
My arrow chains and severs upon all those that can barely access The First Tongue!

This terrifying Thesis allowed for an utterly horrendous and ruthless action to occur as the arrow warped through space to find its next target, an Intermediate Depth Spirit whose form resembled a writhing mass of ethereal tentacles, and it pierced through that existence with the same casual ease before chaining to the next target and the next and the next!
Eight THE Intermediate Depth Spirits.
Thirty-six THE Surface Depth Spirits.

The arrow moved through them like it was popping bubbles, multiple sounds echoing out across existence as a single projectile pierced dozens of Civilizations in sequence, leaving behind dim eyes and collapsing Ways as it carved a path of devastation through the forces of THE Living Spirit!
Pop.
Pop.
Pop!
POP!!!

Its body was massive and serpentine, scales of gray-white spirit essence covering a form that stretched for miles, with jaws that could have swallowed small realms and eyes that blazed with the fury of oceanic depths that had never known sunlight.

It roared as its Way of Spirit Water tried to make a stand against the arrow that had materialized before its existence, ancient Principles activating in desperate defense as Declarations attempted to form around its body like shields.
But an earlier Thesis had already cut off its access to The First Tongue.
And this arrow carried a Thesis that built upon that previous Thesis while holding a weight no Intermediate Depth entity could truly withstand!

The Cetus had been Fundamental, had stood at heights that would have made it nearly untouchable under normal circumstances, but currently it was dragged down to Intermediate by the Fragment’s power, and what occurred next was just utter devastation of a Way!
It seemed like a long time, but all of this was happening in a fraction of a femtosecond.

The arrow burning with Thesis pierced across the Cetus with the ease of a blade through mist, its blue-gold radiance carving through spirit essence and Way alike as if they were made of paper rather than the accumulated authority of eons.

The great serpentine form shuddered once, twice, and then its Way shattered like glass struck by a hammer, fragments of Spirit Water scattering across Muspelheim in a display that would have been beautiful if it were not so terrible.

Its Civilization collapsed in the same instant, the connections it had built over countless years severing all at once as its existence ceased to be anything more than resources waiting to be harvested.
And then the arrow flew ever faster.
It did not stop with a single kill.
My arrow chains and severs upon all those that can barely access The First Tongue!

This terrifying Thesis allowed for an utterly horrendous and ruthless action to occur as the arrow warped through space to find its next target, an Intermediate Depth Spirit whose form resembled a writhing mass of ethereal tentacles, and it pierced through that existence with the same casual ease before chaining to the next target and the next and the next!
Eight THE Intermediate Depth Spirits.
Thirty-six THE Surface Depth Spirits.

The arrow moved through them like it was popping bubbles, multiple sounds echoing out across existence as a single projectile pierced dozens of Civilizations in sequence, leaving behind dim eyes and collapsing Ways as it carved a path of devastation through the forces of THE Living Spirit!
Pop.
Pop.
Pop!
POP!!!

chapters.title: Chapter 4726: Against A Legend! III
paragraphs: Each sound was a Civilization ending, a Way shattering, an existence that had accumulated power over eons being reduced to nothing more than harvest waiting to be claimed.
And then the arrow warped one final time to appear before the eyes of a scrambling Gal’Thûrak in the skies!

The demon spirit’s seven eyes went wide with horror and fear that he had not felt in eons, his chains rattling uselessly at his sides as he recognized that death had come for him in the form of a blue-gold arrow that had just murdered his colleagues without slowing down.
"PLEASE!"

His roar was desperate and pathetic, the sound of someone who had spent his existence subjugating others suddenly finding himself on the other end of absolute power, and the terror in his voice was so raw and so genuine that it might have moved a lesser being to mercy.
Noah was not a lesser being.
But in the next moment, as the arrow surged toward Gal’Thûrak with the inevitability of a death sentence already signed, a massive white-gray claw appeared in its path!

THE Living Spirit moved with speed that defied even the slowed perception of this moment, one of his countless limbs extending across the distance between himself and his subordinate as he refused to lose another...well, actually, the last follower to this impossible enemy!

The claw was massive and terrible, composed of compressed spirits that screamed silently as they were forced into service, and it caught the arrow with a grip that released gray bursts of Immensity in all directions.
"SPIRITS CANNOT BE SEVERED BY MORTAL WEAPONS!"
BOOM!

The Declaration crashed against Noah’s Thesis with the weight of someone who had been ancient when THE Fallout was merely a possibility rather than a reality, and the arrow holding the terrifying Thesis buzzed in THE Living Spirit’s deformed and radiant claw as two authorities contested for dominance.
The arrow stopped.

THE Living Spirit looked toward Noah with eyes that blazed with fury beyond anything he had shown before, with rage that spoke of losses that could not be calculated and insults that could not be forgiven.
And then he looked past Noah, toward the surroundings of the citadel where his forces had been stationed.
All of them had slumped down like dolls whose strings had been cut.

The Cetus. The tentacled horror. The eight Intermediate Depth spirits. The thirty-six Surface Depth entities. All of them lay still and silent, their Ways shattered and their Civilizations collapsed, nothing remaining but corpses that had once been legends in their own right.
An instant later, those corpses began to move.

They flew out toward Noah as if drawn by invisible strings, rising from where they had fallen and streaming through the burning air of Muspelheim toward the entity who had killed them, and one by one, they sank into his back with sounds like stones dropping into still water.
As each one was drawn into him, Noah’s immensity and weight erupted higher and higher!
The first corpse, a Surface Depth spirit, added its essence to his foundation.
The second and third and fourth followed, each one making him burn brighter.
THE Intermediate Depth spirits came next, their accumulated authority flooding into his existence with force that made the air around him shimmer and distort.

And finally, the Cetus, the former Fundamental Depth entity whose Way of Spirit Water had been shattered by a single arrow, sank into his back and elevated his foundation in ways that made everything before seem like appetizers before a feast!

Blue-gold flames surrounded Noah in a corona of power that seemed to grow with every corpse he absorbed, making him look glorious and tyrannical in ways that defied easy description. He had just collapsed dozens of Civilizations in a single blow. He had collapsed a Fundamental Depth entity in a single blow! Even if he was utilizing a Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem to reduce their Depths, even if he had built his attack on an already established Thesis, the achievement was staggering!
What a terrifying wonder he had become!

He carried out such a ruthless action with the casual ease of someone who had long since stopped feeling guilt for doing what needed to be done, and in the heavy silence that followed, prompts bloomed before him with comprehensive detail!
|Mass Harvest Report|
|Civilizations Collapsed: 45|
|Breakdown:|
|THE Fundamental Depth of Absolute Sovereignty (Spirit Water - Cetus Variant): 1|

|As directed, everything about this entity has been transformed into Harvest that is amplified and devoured to elevate your Foundation and Way. Its accumulated authority over eons, its Principles of oceanic depth and spirit essence, its connections and its knowledge and its very existence have all been converted into fuel for your advancement.|
|THE Intermediate Depth of Absolute Sovereignty: 8|
|8 entities have been transformed into the optimum loot of 12 Fragments of Moirai Threads.|
|Current Moirai Thread Fragment Count: Previous + 12. Full Simulation till death possible.|
|THE Surface Depth of Absolute Sovereignty: 36|

|All 36 entities have had everything about them transformed into Harvest that is amplified and devoured to elevate your Foundation and Way. They didn’t have much individually, but quantity has a quality all its own.|

|Foundation Status: Burning. Your comparative Weight, even while not being entirely accurate in its capabilities due to your Formless Depth, is rising comparably to be 70/100th the Immensity of THE Creature and THE Primordial Chaos at Intermediate Depth.|
|Current Comparative Weight: Approximately 70/100th.|
BOOM!

Noah floated in the burning skies of Muspelheim as an imposing humanoid figure whose weight and immensity bellowed around him like a declaration of war against everything that dared to oppose him, and he stared up toward THE Living Spirit with eyes that blazed through the flames surrounding his form.
Those flames.

Those billowing blue-gold flames of Primus Mana that surrounded him made him seem like a flaming entity whose face could barely be observed through the conflagration, a being of fire and fury and absolute authority whose features were glimpsed only in fragments between the dancing tongues of power that wreathed his entire existence.

The weight burning from him was so immense that reality itself seemed to bend around his presence, the air distorting and the flames of Muspelheim leaning toward him as if paying homage to something that burned hotter and brighter than their eternal fires could ever hope to match.

And when he breathed, one could see furious blue-gold flames rushing from his nose and mouth with every exhale, fire that spoke of power so concentrated that it could not be contained within a mere physical form!

He looked like a wild celestial humanoid beast, something that had crawled out of the primordial fires that existed before existence learned to cool, and the flames billowing from his nose and mouth emanated so much heat that it truly felt like these flames alone could utterly scorch to cinders any THE Surface Depth Civilizations just by being near!
The very act of his breathing had become a threat!
The very fact of his existence had become a Declaration!
Oh!

chapters.title: Chapter 4727: All Things Live And Die I
paragraphs: All beings rose to power.

THE Creature rose to power as he was THE Intermediate Depth once, climbing through the stages of Absolute Sovereignty like everyone else before reaching heights that made him synonymous with existence itself. So was THE Living Paradox and THE Primordial Chaos, both of them having passed through the lower Depths before ascending to the peaks they currently occupied!

So when it was stated that Noah had 70/100th the power of THE Living Paradox or THE Creature at Intermediate Depth, this was only a point of comparison for them at that specific stage of their journey!
Would the immensity of any common Intermediate Depth entity even come close to matching the immensity of THE Creature at Intermediate Depth?
The answer was a clear and resounding no.

THE Creature at Intermediate Depth had already been a monster beyond monsters, a being whose foundation was so profound and whose accumulation was so vast that comparing him to ordinary Intermediate Depth entities was like comparing an ocean to a puddle. The same was true for THE Living Paradox and THE Primordial Chaos, beings who had been exceptional even at lower Depths, whose foundations had been built on concepts so fundamental that their immensity dwarfed their supposed peers.

It was estimated that at most, a powerful Intermediate Depth entity, the renowned beings who had grand Civilizations and who had built up their foundations to the absolute peak as they waited for a spark to enter Fundamental Depth, such entities could maybe come close to matching a tenth of what the immensity of THE Creature had been at that stage.
And even that estimate could be off!

This was the power that Noah currently held as he continued rising through the burning skies of Muspelheim, his form wreathed in blue-gold flames that made him look less like a man and more like a celestial phenomenon given consciousness and purpose.

He came to float on the same level as THE Living Spirit, the two of them facing each other across a distance that seemed both vast and insignificant at the same time, predator meeting predator in the eternal dance of those who refused to acknowledge anything as superior to themselves.
The two looked at each other dangerously.

THE Living Spirit’s form had shifted from the amorphous mass of countless spirits into something more defined, more intentional, a humanoid shape that suggested he was taking this confrontation seriously enough to consolidate his presence into a singular expression of power. His face, if it could be called that, held contained calmness and immensity that spoke of eons of existence and countless battles survived.
His voice came out slow and heavy, each word carrying the weight of mountains settling into place.
"Are you him?"
HUUUM!
A simple question that resonated through the burning air of Muspelheim with implications that stretched far beyond its three words.

One that Noah remained nonchalant to as blue-gold flames spilled out of his mouth with every syllable and scorched the surroundings, his Weight and Immensity still acclimating to the massive influx of harvested essence as he replied with casual dismissiveness.

"Such a question could have so many answers, big guy." The flames around him danced with amusement that matched his tone. "But what is this? Are you feeling talkative? I thought we would fight first, establish a baseline, and have a talk after. Preferably as your Way is collapsing."

They began to converse, but it occurred so rapidly that not even a nanosecond had passed or would pass for them anytime soon, their exchange happening in the spaces between moments where lesser beings could not perceive or participate.

And Noah affirmed the effects of the Fragment of THE Axiom of Mayhem that had dimmed in his existence, running calculations through his mind as he assessed that the Depth reduction would last at least a few minutes conservatively and up to an hour or more moderately!
So he looked upon this Legend with eyes that burned with blue-gold fire, and as he watched, their body became more clear, more defined, more intentional in its presentation.

The amalgamation of spirits that had composed THE Living Spirit’s previous form consolidated into a humanoid muscular entity that stood imposing against the backdrop of Muspelheim’s eternal flames. His skin was gray and white, shifting between the two colors in patterns that seemed to follow rules that had nothing to do with normal biology, and multiple shining gray eyes were scattered across different parts of his body, on his shoulders and his chest and his forearms, each one tracking Noah with independent awareness.

He looked alien and off-putting in ways that transcended simple aesthetics, a being that had emerged from concepts that predated the forms most entities wore, but despite this strangeness, he possessed his own sense of regality that could not be denied.
He looked at Noah closely, those countless gray eyes examining him up and down with scrutiny that missed nothing.

"Your usage of ancient power. Your Declaration with The First Tongue." His voice was measured and analytical now, the tone of someone piecing together a puzzle that had just become far more interesting than expected. "Are you the one who has claimed THE First Tongue? And still currently emerging? Still weak?"
His eyes narrowed with understanding that was equal parts respect and predatory interest.
"It is why you did what you did with my forces, but you had to rely on a Fragment of an Axiom to give yourself an edge?"
The words were heavy with implications as Noah’s eyes shone sharply.
He tilted his head and spoke with flames licking around his words.

"Do those within THE Loom not communicate? Do you not know about me?"His smile was sharp enough to cut. "Or did THE Living Paradox keep information about me to his closest dogs, and you did not make the cut as one of the dogs who licks him the most? Because even THE Living Elemental seems closer to Paradox..."
Noah’s words burned with brilliance that made the air itself recoil, each syllable a calculated strike at pride that had existed for eons beyond counting.

THE Living Spirit continued to look at him calmly, absorbing the insult without visible reaction, before his voice emerged imposing and ominous in ways that made the eternal flames of Muspelheim seem to dim.

"Maybe information was withheld about you because of what you represent." His countless eyes gleamed with hunger that could not be disguised. "THE Living Paradox would gain much for eating the one who claimed THE First Tongue. So would Elemental and many others. I wouldn’t blame them for not sharing such information."
He paused, and something that might have been a smile crossed his alien features.
"Just like they wouldn’t blame me for the fact that I won’t be telling anyone about your appearance here. I would want you... all to myself."
His form seemed to grow more solid, more present, more real as he spoke his ambitions aloud.

"After all, the benefits to usurping One Who Laid A Claim are many. Just look at THE Living Paradox and the heights he has reached."His eyes blazed with dreams that had suddenly become possibilities. "Can you imagine it, Youngest Claimer? THE Living Spirit eating you and joining the ranks of THE Creature and THE Living Paradox?"
BOOM!

His eyes shone with an ominous and terrifying light that spoke of hunger and ambition and the willingness to do whatever was necessary to achieve heights that had seemed impossible just moments before, and Noah’s visage frowned even as a devilish smile curved across his features.
The flames billowing around him became more controlled, more focused, more intentional as he responded to the threat with calm that bordered on arrogance.

"Are you sure about that?" His voice carried the weight of someone who had heard such threats before and remained standing while those who made them had long since ceased to exist. "It is ambitious. This can also play to my favor. You tell nobody about me here, and I get to potentially collapse THE great Living Spirit with nobody being the wiser."
He floated forward slightly, his flames reaching toward THE Living Spirit like eager servants.
"Can you imagine that, O Weakest of THE Emerged Leaders?"

His words were heavy with mockery that cut deeper than any blade, but THE Living Spirit’s eyes smiled dangerously in response, countless gray orbs crinkling with amusement that spoke of someone who enjoyed the game even as the stakes rose to lethal heights.

"Existence is all about risks." THE Living Spirit nodded with the gravity of someone who had gambled with his existence countless times and won."I assure you that I take you very seriously the moment I affirmed your identity. Anybody that has laid a claim is not a normal entity. I expect you to be slippery. I expect you to be hard."
His form pulsed with power that made the air around them both grow heavy.
"But hey, such is existence."
His smile widened, revealing teeth that seemed to be made of compressed spirits screaming in silent agony.
"And you didn’t think you were the only one who could play around with Fragments of Axioms, right? Even with my Depth slightly reduced, with enough power..."
His voice dropped to something almost gentle, almost caring, almost horrifying in its false concern.

"I worry for you, O Youngest Claimer. I truly, truly worry for your safety. Come, let me invite you to an endless slumber inside an Infinite Spiritual Depth. There, you can dream of The First Tongue while I will actualize it for you."
Noah’s expression remained valiant and calm even as in the next moment, above THE Living Spirit, a terrifying singularity bloomed into existence with force that made reality itself groan in protest!

A gray scythe began to manifest from that singularity, its blade curved with the promise of endings that could not be avoided and its handle wrapped in chains of spiritual essence that writhed with tortured awareness. The weapon was massive and terrible, designed not for combat but for harvesting, for reaping, for claiming the existence of those unfortunate enough to stand before its edge.
And it manifested with the light of a Fragment of an Axiom!
Noah’s eyes flashed sharply as he recognized what he was seeing!
He had expected one of THE Living Existences to have tools up their sleeves as a Fragment of an Axiom was one such tool, but still, it seemed like things would not be made easy for him!

Because that Fragment blooming above THE Living Spirit shone with the splendor of a Paradoxical Axiom, the essence of contradiction itself woven into a weapon that could probably do things that defied normal understanding of what was possible!
But he remained calm.
Because at this moment, from below, two auras of Fundamental Depth neared his position with speed.
The Muspeli Giants.
The ones who had been holding back the weight of the previous Half-Step Absolute Depth THE Living Spirit before Noah’s Fragment had reduced him to peak Fundamental!
